reason: Cohesive router: six endpoints for one resource sharing maybeUserId, gateAuthed and callResumeBinding, plus inline zod-openapi schemas that inflate the line count without adding branching. Splitting it needs characterization tests first (this skill's own rule) and the lane's suggested cut point is unusable — its symbol map reports impossible spans (callResumeBinding at 807-1029 in a then-970-line file; maybeUserId as 574 lines when it is ~11), because it measures distance to the next function keyword and swallows the intervening app.openapi route registrations. Reported separately as a detector bug. Not splitting a live app's only jobs router on a broken cut suggestion; the 180-day expiry and the >20% hard-reopen are the right leash.

This is the whole micro-frontend's style surface in one file, already navigable: 14 banner-comment sections, and the build concatenates to a single dist/style.css regardless, so splitting buys no load-graph benefit and no readability the banners do not already give. CSS also carries none of the size lane's usual risk — no branching, no untested logic — and the real gates on it are lint:css plus the @wolffm/themes check-usage token check, both green. Splitting is mechanical but touches every selector in a live app for zero functional gain, which is a bad trade to make speculatively. Revisit if it crosses roughly 2000 lines or gains a second consumer; the >20% hard-reopen catches the first case automatically.
